questions.markdown:
A solid circular bar of length $L = 1.2\ \text{m}$ tapers linearly from diameter $d_1 = 30\ \text{mm}$ (large end) to $d_2 = 20\ \text{mm}$ (small end). The bar is loaded in tension with an axial load $P = 40\ \text{kN}$. The material has yield strength 250 MPa and Young's modulus $E = 200\ \text{GPa}$.

Determine:

i) The axial (working) stress at the large and small ends.\nii) The factor of safety against yielding based on the maximum stress.\nThe total change in length (elongation) of the tapered bar under the load.

A surgeon requires that the inner diameter at C be 10.0 mm for a medical purpose. The bone at C will carry an axial tensile load of 1500 N and the allowable average normal stress (from the strain gauge limit) is 3.20 MPa. The modulus of elasticity of the bone material is 18 GPa, and the effective length of the loaded bone section is 200 mm. A factor of safety (F.S.) = 1.5 must also be considered in the design. Determine the minimum outer diameter required at C (in mm) so that average stress does not exceed the allowable and the elongation of the bone section under the applied load.

diagrams.caption: Bone diagram with axial loads of 1500 N at both ends and section C marked. (original source region)

questions.markdown: A bar of 25 mm diameter is tested in tension. It is observed that when a load of 60kN is applied, the extension measured over a gauge length of 200 mm is 0.12 mm and the contraction in diameter is 0.0045 mm. Determine Poisson's ratio and elastic constants $E$, $G$, $K$.

A cylindrical shell 3m long, which is closed at the ends, has an internal diameter of 1.5m and a wall thickness of 20mm. Determine the circumferential and longitudinal stresses induced, and the change in the dimensions of the steel. If it is subjected to an internal pressure of 1.5 N/mm2. Take $E=2\times10^5\,\text{N/mm}^2$ and Poisson's ratio=0.3

Three bars made of copper, zinc and aluminium are of equal length and have cross-sections 500, 750 and 1000 square mm, respectively. They are rigidly connected at their ends. If the compound member is subjected to a longitudinal pull of 250 kN. Determine the proportion of the load carried by each rod and the induced stresses. Take the value of $E$ for copper = $1.3\times10^5\ \text{N/mm}^2$, for zinc = $1.0\times10^5\ \text{N/mm}^2$ and for aluminium = $0.8\times10^5\ \text{N/mm}^2$.

diagrams.caption: Compound bar diagram with copper, zinc, and aluminium rods carrying load P = 250 kN. (original source region)
